about: The lab's work list (chapter 10), in priority order. An item is done only when its proof test exists and passes: node tools/progress.mjs checks that the test exists, and node check.mjs runs it. Work on one item at a time. Change an item's status and proof; never delete or reword an item to make the list look finished.

features.description: The helpdesk's routes, services and data layer stay in order, enforced by import rules whose failure messages say how to fix the violation.
A refused or cut-off model response can't pass as a finished answer.
The triage assistant's loop stops at its turn limit.
The triage assistant's tools only read (two until chapter 11 added a third).
The API contract is generated from the code, and a contract that falls behind fails with the change named.
A script lists the evidence a repository's files give for each part of a harness.
features.proof: tools/harness-inventory.test.mjs::every kind of evidence is found and named

features.description: Checks of properties of the code as a whole: every route declares its response model, tests fake the model client, and no read route returns a customer's email.
Only helpdesk.model imports the model vendor's SDK, enforced by an allow-list rule that covers modules written after it.
The TypeScript package keeps its layers and its Node-only code in the CLI, checked by ESLint and dependency-cruiser, and both checks read every file.
features.proof: ts/test/boundaries.test.ts::reads every TypeScript file in the package

features.description: Code reads a model's text through final_text, enforced by the lab's own lint rule, whose exceptions must each give a reason.
The command-line tool's output goes through write, enforced by a custom ESLint rule that fixes what is safe to fix.
features.proof: ts/test/lint-rules.test.ts::fixes a console.log planted in the CLI's run() back to write()

features.description: The triage assistant is defined as data and checked against the platform's policy before it runs, with fixtures that specify every rule.
Every guard from chapters 16 to 18 is broken on purpose every night, and a test must catch each; the runner checks its own controls.
features.proof: tools/mutate.test.mjs::a mutation the test notices is caught, and the file is put back

features.description: When a coding agent says it's done, the fast checks run, and a failure goes back to it with what failed, how to rerun it and what doesn't count as a fix, at most three times in a row.
features.proof: tools/hooks/stop-check.test.mjs::after three blocks in a row, lets the agent stop and tells the person

features.description: A headless loop gives failing checks to an agent command with a cap on attempts, and stops early when an attempt changes nothing or when the agent changes the checks.
features.proof: tools/fix-loop.test.mjs::stops when the agent changes the checks, and leaves the change for a person

features.description: A script reads a repository's git history and shows, by folder, how often fixes landed on recent agent work and how long after the change, with bookkeeping files left out.
features.proof: tools/rework.test.mjs::a fix to a file an agent changed days before is rework, counted in that file's folder

features.description: The assistant searches the knowledge base with keyword and vector rankings fused by rank, measured by recall at 3 on a golden set that fails below its floor, and every citation in its answer is checked against the passages it was given.

The triage assistant's tools act for one member of staff and refuse what that person can't see, check every argument against a strict schema before running, answer a bad call with what to do next, and return long lists a page at a time.
The assistant can draft a reply to a ticket, which a person reads before anything is sent.
Sending a reply or closing a ticket waits for a person's approval (chapter 19).

An agent definition that gives its agent a tool that changes things must say whose approval each change needs, at least what the platform's policy requires, and the tool can't be built without it (chapter 19).

Before a coding agent runs a shell command that would destroy work no commit holds, a hook asks the person where Claude Code can show a prompt and denies where it can't, and fails closed; deny rules refuse force pushes in every mode (chapter 19).
features.proof: tools/hooks/destructive-guard.test.mjs::where a person can see a prompt the guard asks; where none can be shown it denies and says why

features.description: An MCP server offers the helpdesk's read tools to any MCP client (chapter 12).

The MCP server serves HTTP as an OAuth resource server: it accepts only tokens issued for it alone, requires each operation's scope, acts for the person the token names, never passes the token on and audits every request; and it runs only as the catalog of approved servers approved it (chapter 13).

An orchestrator hands each customer's tickets to a worker with its own context and counts in code what came back, whatever its own summary says; a draft goes back to be revised until the citation check passes, at most three rounds; and what each design sends to the model is measured (chapter 14).

What a customer writes reaches the assistant as data, instruction-shaped text is flagged for the person who approves, and a model that obeys an injected ticket changes nothing, flagged or not: its tools act for one person, a change waits for approval, and nothing it can reach sends anything outside (chapter 20).
Every Python and npm download is checked against a hash recorded in a lock file, the helpdesk builds without fetching anything unchecked, and what is installed matches the locks (chapter 20).
features.proof: tools/lockfiles.test.mjs::setup.mjs must require hashes and build without fetching

features.description: Models are components with retirement dates (agents/models.toml): a definition naming a model that has retired, is deprecated or may retire within the policy's notice fails, with the date and what to move to, and every model the code names is a pinned ID (chapter 20).
The catalog pins a digest of the tool definitions an MCP server was approved with, and the server refuses to start when a description has changed since (chapter 20).

Golden sets of tasks for the assistant, each with a key of properties rather than words: facts graded against what the run's own tools returned, what it must never say, the proposals it must file, and citations; several trials a task with pass@k and pass^k; and a check that every reference passes and every scripted mistake fails (chapter 21).

A model judge grades the assistant's drafts against a rubric, one criterion a call, against the tool results the writer was given; every verdict is checked against a schema and a malformed one is an error, never a pass; the judge is calibrated against a person's labels with false passes counted apart; and a judge in the revise loop stops at the round limit (chapter 22).
The golden sets and the judge gate a change: a regression suite in CI, a promotion gate, and what each run costs (chapter 23).

The harness is measured against a baseline: rule violations, CI pass rate on agent changes, rework and reverts, cost per merged change and drift incidents, with the AI calls' tokens, cost and failures recorded (chapter 26).
features.proof: tools/measure.test.mjs::--against reports both windows, uses the baseline's length and known failures, and says what's noise

features.description: Every model call goes through one gateway that holds the keys, limits rates and tokens, routes by cost and capability, caches, falls back, and attributes cost to a team (chapter 27).
